scenario_en: We expose POST /webhooks/article-published so publishers can push new articles, and the endpoint is reachable by anyone on the internet.
q: webhook 端点该怎么挡住伪造和垃圾推送？
q_en: How should the webhook endpoint block spoofed and spam pushes?
options: 给每家发布方发密钥或 API key 并逐次校验
只要走 HTTPS 加密传输就能确认来源身份
不做校验就先入库，事后再靠人工抽查删掉垃圾内容
只看请求体里的发布方名字字段来判断是谁推的
options_en: Issue each publisher a shared secret or API key and verify it on every push.
Rely on HTTPS transport encryption alone to establish who the caller is.
Skip verification, ingest everything, and rely on manual spot-checks to delete spam.
Trust the publisher name field inside the request body to identify the caller.
codeSample:
POST /webhooks/article-published HTTP/1.1
X-API-Key: pub_cnn_9f3a...        # 每家发布方一把，可单独吊销
Content-Type: application/json

{"url":"...","title":"...","published_at":"2024-06-21T22:30:00Z"}
why: 加密只保证链路上没人偷看，认证才回答"这是谁推的"；每家一把密钥还能在泄漏时单独吊销。代价是要和上千家发布方分发并轮换密钥。
why_en: Encryption only stops eavesdropping — authentication is what answers who pushed this, and a per-publisher key can be revoked alone when it leaks.
whenOtherWins: 如果推送方全在内网且网络边界可信，IP 白名单比分发密钥更省运维。
tradeoff: 共享密钥的可吊销身份 vs 密钥分发轮换的运维负担

termDefinitions.meaning: 发给调用方的一串凭据，请求时带上用来证明身份。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An API key is a credential string issued to a caller and sent with each request to prove identity.

termDefinitions.meaning: 加密传输的 HTTP，保证链路内容不被窃听或篡改。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: HTTPS is HTTP over an encrypted channel so traffic cannot be read or tampered with in transit.

optionExplanations: 对，凭据放在请求头里逐次校验，来路不明的推送在入队之前就被拒掉。
加密解决的是"有没有人偷看"，跟"对面是不是 CNN"完全是两个问题。
事后人工清理跟不上推送速率，垃圾内容会先出现在用户 feed 里。
请求体里的字段是调用方自己写的，任何人都能随便填一个发布方名字。
optionExplanations_en: Right — the credential rides in the header and is checked per call, so unknown senders are rejected before anything is queued.
Encryption answers whether anyone is eavesdropping, a different question from whether the caller really is CNN.
Manual cleanup cannot keep up with push rates, so spam reaches user feeds first.
Body fields are written by the caller, so anyone can type in any publisher name they like.

scenario: 个性化 feed 为每个用户预先算好，存在 feed:user:12345，后台 worker 在新文章到达时按相关性慢慢往里加。
scenario_en: Personalized feeds are precomputed for each individual reader in feed:user:12345, and background workers slowly add new articles by relevance score.
q: 除了内存开销，per-user 预计算 feed 还会在什么时候出错？
q_en: Beyond memory cost, when else does a per-user precomputed feed go wrong?
options: 兴趣变了 feed 仍是旧偏好，突发要闻也可能缺席
用户翻页时会拿到完全随机排序的历史文章列表
分类缓存会被个性化 worker 定期整块删除掉
文章的发布时间戳会被 worker 在写入时改写
options_en: Interests shift but the feed still reflects old preferences, and breaking news can be missing entirely.
Paging returns a completely randomly ordered list of historical articles.
Category caches get periodically wiped wholesale by the personalization worker.
Publish timestamps get rewritten by the worker as it writes entries.
why: 预计算把排序挪到写路径，feed 只反映上一次计算时的画像；全民该看到的突发新闻如果不在这个人的相关性列表里，就永远不会被塞进去。
why_en: Precomputing moves ranking to the write path, so the feed reflects only the profile at the last computation, and a globally important story never enters a feed whose score misses it.
optionExplanations: 对，画像变化和全局要闻这两件事都发生在预计算之后，缓存里没有就补不上。
排序恰恰是预计算时按相关性分数定好的，结果是固定顺序而不是随机。
分类缓存由采集侧的 feed worker 维护，个性化流程只读它，不负责清理。
时间戳来自采集时解析到的发布时间，个性化 worker 只拿它当排序输入。
optionExplanations_en: Right — both the profile shift and the global story happen after precomputation, and what is not in the cache cannot be filled in.
Ordering is exactly what precomputation fixes by relevance score, giving a stable order rather than a random one.
Category caches are maintained by ingest-side feed workers; personalization only reads them.
Timestamps come from the publish time parsed at ingest; the personalization worker only uses them as a ranking input.

scenario: 个性化改成用几 KB 的偏好向量在请求时混合分类 feed：60% technology、30% business、10% trending。
scenario_en: Personalization becomes a few-KB preference vector that mixes category feeds on demand: 60% technology, 30% business, 10% trending.
q: 这套按比例混合分类 feed 的方案要付什么代价？
q_en: What does this ratio-based category mixing approach cost?
options: 个性化只到分类粒度，窄兴趣漏要闻、宽兴趣显泛化
内存占用会比给每个用户存一份缓存还要大得多
所有分类 feed 都必须改回实时数据库查询才能混合
每个用户的偏好向量里必须完整存下 1000 篇文章
options_en: Personalization only reaches category granularity: narrow interests miss big stories, broad ones feel generic.
Memory usage ends up far larger than storing one cache per user.
Every category feed must revert to real-time database queries to be mixable.
Each user's preference vector must store a full 1,000 articles.
why: 混合只能在几百个分类 feed 之间调比例，换来内存降两个数量级；代价是深度不足，需要专门调多样性兜住窄兴趣和宽兴趣两头。
why_en: Mixing only tunes ratios across a few hundred category feeds, which cuts memory by two orders of magnitude but costs depth, so diversity has to be tuned deliberately.
whenOtherWins: 如果用户量小到给每人存一份缓存也扛得住，per-user 预计算能给出更细的个性化。
tradeoff: 分类混合的低内存成本 vs 逐用户排序的个性化深度
optionExplanations: 对，比例只落在分类上，同一分类内部谁排前面就没法再按个人偏好区分。
偏好向量只有几 KB，缓存数量从上亿降到几百，内存方向恰好相反。
这套方案正建立在分类 feed 已经预计算好之上，混合的是缓存不是查询。
向量存的是各分类的权重比例，文章本身留在共享的分类缓存里。
optionExplanations_en: Right — ratios only apply at the category level, so within one category personal taste can no longer reorder anything.
A preference vector is a few kilobytes and cache count drops from hundreds of millions to hundreds; memory moves the other way.
This design assumes category feeds are already precomputed — what gets mixed is caches, not queries.
The vector holds per-category weights; the articles themselves stay in the shared category caches.

scenario: cursor 从单一 published_at 换成 "2024-01-15T10:30:00Z_article123" 这种时间戳加文章 ID 的复合值。
scenario_en: The cursor changes from a bare published_at to a composite like "2024-01-15T10:30:00Z_article123" carrying timestamp plus article id.
q: 换成复合 cursor 之后要额外付出哪些代价？（多选）
q_en: What extra costs come with switching to a composite cursor? (Select all that apply.)
options: 应用要维护 cursor 的编码和解码逻辑
cursor 字符串变长，来回传输的体积增加
(published_at, article_id) 复合索引要额外存储
数据库从此无法再按 published_at 排序
options_en: The application must maintain encode and decode logic for the cursor.
The cursor string gets longer, so more bytes travel back and forth.
The composite index on (published_at, article_id) needs extra storage.
The database can no longer sort by published_at at all.
why: 复合 cursor 换来同时间戳也不漏文章的稳定全序，代价分摊在三处：多写的编解码代码、更长的游标字符串、以及复合索引占的磁盘。
why_en: A composite cursor buys a stable total order even under identical timestamps, and pays for it in encode/decode code, a longer cursor string, and index disk.
optionExplanations: 两个字段拼进一个字符串，客户端传回来时要拆开还原成元组比较的参数。
游标要在每次翻页请求里往返，长度增加是持续的小额带宽支出。
索引把两列一起排好存一份，这份额外结构是查询变快的实付成本。
排序能力没有丢失，恰恰相反，这个方案就是靠两列一起排序来定序的。
optionExplanations_en: Two fields packed into one string must be split apart again to rebuild the tuple comparison arguments.
The cursor travels on every page request, so extra length is a small but continuous bandwidth cost.
The index stores both columns pre-sorted as a separate structure, and that is the real price of the faster query.
Sorting is not lost — this design works precisely by ordering on both columns together.

scenario: 系统已经上线，文章主键用的是随机 UUID；现在想换成单调递增的 ULID，好让 cursor 只带一个 ID。
scenario_en: The system is live with random UUID article primary keys, and the team now wants monotonic ULIDs so the cursor can be a single id.
q: 已经用随机 UUID 之后再改单调 ID，代价主要在哪？
q_en: What is the main cost of moving to monotonic ids after random UUIDs are already in use?
options: 要做一次带外键引用的主键数据迁移
ULID 在关系型数据库里不能当主键使用
换完之后就再也无法按发布时间排序了
历史文章会在迁移过程中被自动清空掉
options_en: It forces a primary-key data migration that drags foreign-key references along.
ULIDs cannot be used as a primary key in a relational database.
After the switch you can no longer sort by publish time at all.
Historical articles get automatically wiped during the migration.
why: 单调 ID 是最简单的 cursor 方案，但它要求在设计期就定下来；事后迁移要动主键和所有引用它的地方，往往比直接上复合 cursor 更贵。
why_en: Monotonic ids give the simplest cursor but must be chosen up front, because retrofitting them rewrites the primary key and everything referencing it.

termDefinitions.meaning: 通用唯一标识符，通常随机生成，因此不带时间顺序。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Universally Unique Identifier is a typically random identifier that carries no chronological order.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把时间戳放在前缀里的唯一标识符，字典序即大致时间序。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A ULID is a unique identifier whose timestamp prefix makes lexicographic order roughly chronological.

optionExplanations: 对，旧行要重新发号，指向它们的每一处引用都得跟着改，还不能中断写入。
ULID 就是一个定长字符串或 128 位值，当主键完全没有障碍。
published_at 列还在，按时间排序的能力跟主键换不换毫无关系。
迁移是改写标识符而不是删数据，会丢数据的方案本身就不该通过评审。
optionExplanations_en: Right — old rows need renumbering and every reference to them must follow, all without pausing live writes.
A ULID is just a fixed-length string or 128-bit value; nothing stops it from being a primary key.
The published_at column still exists, so sorting by time is unaffected by which primary key you use.
Migration rewrites identifiers rather than deleting rows; a plan that loses data should never pass review.

scenario: 文章由多个采集实例并发写入，而 cursor 分页依赖 article_id 大致按时间递增。
scenario_en: Articles are written concurrently by several ingestion instances, while cursor pagination depends on article_id increasing roughly with time.
q: 多实例并发写入时怎么生成有序 ID 又不卡吞吐？
q_en: How do you generate ordered ids across concurrent writers without capping throughput?
options: 各实例本地生成 ULID，用时间戳前缀保证大致有序
所有实例抢同一个数据库自增列，写入全部串行化
每个实例各自生成随机 UUID，反正保证了唯一性
实例之间每生成一个 ID 都先投票达成一次共识
options_en: Each instance generates ULIDs locally, with the timestamp prefix keeping them roughly ordered.
All instances contend on one database auto-increment column, serializing every write.
Each instance generates random UUIDs on its own, since uniqueness is guaranteed anyway.
Instances run a consensus vote among themselves before every single id they generate.
why: 把时间戳编进 ID 前缀，顺序信息就随 ID 一起本地产生，不需要任何跨实例协调；代价是同一毫秒内跨实例的先后并不严格。
why_en: Encoding the timestamp into the id prefix produces ordering locally with no cross-instance coordination, at the cost of loose ordering within the same millisecond.
whenOtherWins: 如果要求 ID 严格单调且不能有跨实例乱序，就得上中心化发号器，用吞吐上限换严格全序。
tradeoff: 本地生成 ULID 的吞吐 vs 中心化发号器的严格全序

termDefinitions.meaning: 把时间戳放在前缀里的唯一标识符，字典序即大致时间序。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A ULID is a unique identifier whose timestamp prefix makes lexicographic order roughly chronological.

termDefinitions.meaning: 通用唯一标识符，通常随机生成，因此不带时间顺序。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Universally Unique Identifier is a typically random identifier that carries no chronological order.

optionExplanations: 对，顺序来自 ID 自身的时间前缀，写入路径上没有需要排队的共享资源。
共享自增列会把所有采集实例挤到一个写点上，吞吐直接被单点限死。
随机值只解决唯一性，拿它当 cursor 翻页会得到毫无意义的顺序。
为每条数据跑一轮共识，延迟按网络往返计，高频采集写完全承受不起。
optionExplanations_en: Right — order comes from the id's own time prefix, so the write path shares no resource that needs queuing.
A shared auto-increment column funnels every ingestion instance through one write point, capping throughput there.
Random values only give uniqueness; using them as a paging cursor yields a meaningless order.
Running consensus per row costs a network round trip each time, which high-rate ingestion cannot absorb.

scenario: 区域 feed 存在 Redis sorted set feed:US 里，团队想让每篇文章各自在 30 分钟后消失，好控制这个 key 的大小。
scenario_en: The regional feed lives in a Redis sorted set feed:US, and the team wants each article to expire on its own after 30 minutes to bound the key size.
q: Redis sorted set 能给单个成员设过期时间吗？
q_en: Can a Redis sorted set expire an individual member?
options: 不能，TTL 只作用在整个 key，成员级要靠排名裁剪
能，用 EXPIRE 直接对 sorted set 的某个成员设置
能，把 score 换成过期时间戳，Redis 会自动清理
能，为每篇文章单独建 key 并挂进同一个 sorted set
options_en: No — TTL applies to the whole key, so member-level bounding needs rank trimming.
Yes — call EXPIRE directly on one member of the sorted set.
Yes — set the score to an expiry timestamp and Redis cleans up automatically.
Yes — give each article its own key and hang it inside the same sorted set.
codeSample:
ZADD feed:US 1719000000 article:123        # score = 发布时间戳
ZREMRANGEBYRANK feed:US 0 -2001            # 只保留最新 2000 篇
EXPIRE feed:US 1800                        # TTL 只能挂在整个 key 上
why: Redis 的过期机制注册在 key 上，sorted set 成员没有独立生命周期；所以 CDC 方案改用 ZADD 之后立刻裁掉最旧的，用固定条数代替过期时间控制大小。
why_en: Redis registers expiry on keys, not on sorted set members, so the CDC design bounds size by trimming right after each write to keep a fixed number of newest entries.

termDefinitions.meaning: 缓存条目的存活时长，到期后自动被清除。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Time To Live is how long a cache entry survives before it is automatically evicted.

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis 里按 score 排序的集合结构，支持按排名或按分数范围读写。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A sorted set is a Redis structure ordered by score that supports reads by rank or by score range.

termDefinitions.meaning: 变更数据捕获：把数据库的行级变更实时转成事件流供下游消费。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Change Data Capture turns row-level database changes into a real-time event stream for downstream consumers.

optionExplanations: 对，所以大小要靠"只保留最新 N 篇"这种按排名裁剪的方式来兜。
EXPIRE 的参数是 key 名，Redis 根本没有接受成员参数的过期命令。
score 只决定排序位置，Redis 不会去解读它的语义并据此删成员。
成员是字符串不是 key 引用，独立的 key 过期不会让它从集合里消失。
optionExplanations_en: Right — so size is bounded by rank trimming, keeping only the newest N entries.
EXPIRE takes a key name; Redis has no expiry command that accepts a member argument at all.
Score only decides ordering position; Redis never interprets its meaning to delete members.
Members are strings, not key references, so expiring a separate key does not remove them from the set.

q: 把区域 feed 的 cache-aside 读路径按顺序排列：
q_en: Put the cache-aside read path for a regional feed in order:
steps: Feed Service 先读 Redis 里的 feed:US
未命中时回落数据库，按发布时间查该地区最新文章
把查到的结果写回 Redis 并挂上 30 分钟 TTL
返回给客户端，同一地区的后续请求直接命中缓存
why: cache-aside 由应用自己负责回填：只有 miss 才查库，查完立刻写回。代价是每轮过期后的第一批请求要吃满数据库延迟，集中过期时还会形成惊群。
why_en: In cache-aside the application does the backfill itself: only a miss hits the database, so the first requests after each expiry pay full database latency.

termDefinitions.meaning: 缓存旁路模式：应用先查缓存，未命中时自己查库并把结果写回缓存。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cache-aside means the application checks the cache first and, on a miss, queries the database and writes the result back itself.

termDefinitions.meaning: 缓存条目的存活时长，到期后自动被清除。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Time To Live is how long a cache entry survives before it is automatically evicted.

scenario: 第一页已经从 feed:US 这个 sorted set 读出，客户端带回最后一篇文章的时间戳 1719000000 当 cursor。
scenario_en: The first page has been read from the feed:US sorted set, and the client sends back the last article's timestamp 1719000000 as the cursor.
q: 在 Redis 缓存上继续翻下一页该怎么读？
q_en: How do you fetch the next page directly off the Redis cache?
options: 按 score 严格小于 cursor 做倒序范围读，限制 20 条
按固定排名区间 20 到 39 取出第二页的内容
绕开缓存回落数据库，用 OFFSET 20 LIMIT 20 查
把整个 sorted set 全量取回来后在应用内存里切页
options_en: Do a reverse range read by score strictly below the cursor, limited to 20 entries.
Take the fixed rank window from 20 to 39 as the second page.
Bypass the cache and query the database with OFFSET 20 LIMIT 20.
Pull the entire sorted set back and slice pages in application memory.
codeSample:
ZREVRANGEBYSCORE feed:US (1719000000 -inf LIMIT 0 20
# ( 表示开区间，排除掉 cursor 那一条本身
# score 就是发布时间戳，按 score 翻页 = 按时间翻页
why: score 就是发布时间戳，所以 cursor 分页在缓存层可以原样保留：按分数开区间倒序取下一批，新文章插到顶部也不会推动这个边界。
why_en: Because the score is the publish timestamp, cursor paging carries over to the cache unchanged: a reverse range below the cursor stays stable as new articles land on top.
whenOtherWins: 如果只需要固定的首页而永远不翻页，直接按排名读 ZREVRANGE 0 19 更简单。
tradeoff: 按分数的稳定游标 vs 按排名读取的写法简单

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis 里按 score 排序的集合结构，支持按排名或按分数范围读写。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A sorted set is a Redis structure ordered by score that supports reads by rank or by score range.

optionExplanations: 对，分数边界固定在那一刻的时间戳上，顶部插入多少新文章都影响不到它。
排名会随着新成员插入整体后移，第 20 到 39 名指向的内容一直在变。
缓存里已有现成的有序数据，特意回落数据库等于放弃了这层的全部收益。
一次拉回上千个成员再切页，网络传输和序列化开销都花在没用的部分上。
optionExplanations_en: Right — the score boundary is pinned to that instant, so any number of new articles on top cannot move it.
Ranks shift as new members are inserted, so positions 20 through 39 keep pointing at different content.
The cache already holds ordered data; deliberately falling back to the database throws away this layer entirely.
Fetching a thousand members just to slice one page spends transfer and deserialization cost on data nobody reads.

scenario: 区域 feed 从 TTL 缓存换成事件驱动预计算：数据库变更 → CDC → 消息队列 → feed worker → Redis。
scenario_en: The regional feed moves from TTL caching to event-driven precomputation: database change to CDC to a message queue to feed workers to Redis.
q: 相比 TTL 缓存，这条流水线主要多出什么运维负担？
q_en: Compared with a TTL cache, what operational burden does this pipeline add?
options: CDC、队列、worker 三段都要各自监控和排障
数据库从此不能再接受新文章的写入操作
Redis 必须整个换成关系型存储才能被队列写入
客户端要自己订阅数据库变更来刷新 feed
options_en: CDC, the queue, and the workers each need their own monitoring and debugging.
The database can no longer accept new article writes at all.
Redis must be swapped for relational storage before the queue can write to it.
Clients must subscribe to database changes themselves to refresh the feed.
why: 新鲜度从 30 分钟提到秒级，代价是把一条读路径换成三段有状态链路；任何一段积压或崩掉，缓存都只会静默变旧而不会报错。
why_en: Freshness improves from thirty minutes to seconds by replacing one read path with three stateful stages, and if any stage stalls the cache goes quietly stale.

termDefinitions.meaning: 变更数据捕获：把数据库的行级变更实时转成事件流供下游消费。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Change Data Capture turns row-level database changes into a real-time event stream for downstream consumers.

termDefinitions.meaning: 缓存条目的存活时长，到期后自动被清除。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Time To Live is how long a cache entry survives before it is automatically evicted.

optionExplanations: 对，排查"文章为什么没进 feed"要沿着三处分别看延迟、积压和消费位点。
写入路径完全没变，恰恰是这些写入产生的变更事件驱动了整条流水线。
队列消费者是我们自己的 worker，它拿什么存储写 feed 由我们决定。
客户端只调 feed 接口，数据库变更是内部实现，不该暴露给外部。
optionExplanations_en: Right — diagnosing why an article never reached the feed means checking lag, backlog, and consumer offset in three separate places.
The write path is unchanged; those very writes are what emit the change events driving the pipeline.
The queue consumer is our own worker, so which store it writes the feed into is entirely our choice.
Clients only call the feed endpoint; database changes are an internal detail that should not be exposed.

scenario: 重大新闻发生时，几十家发布方会在同一分钟里向 /webhooks/article-published 集中推送。
scenario_en: When a big story breaks, dozens of publishers push to /webhooks/article-published within the same minute.
q: webhook 端点该怎么扛住这种同时到达的尖峰？
q_en: How should the webhook endpoint absorb this simultaneous spike?
options: 校验后立刻入队返回 200，处理放到队列后面异步做
在请求里同步跑完入库和缓存更新之后再返回 200
超出当前处理能力的推送一律返回 500 让对方重试
限制每家发布方每小时只允许推送固定的若干次
options_en: Validate, enqueue, and return 200 immediately, doing the work asynchronously behind the queue.
Run ingestion and cache updates synchronously inside the request before returning 200.
Reject anything beyond current capacity with a 500 and let the caller retry.
Cap each publisher at a fixed number of pushes per hour.
why: webhook 的调用时机由发布方决定，尖峰形状我们控制不了；端点只做认证和入队就返回，把处理速率交给队列后面的 worker 平滑。
why_en: Publishers decide when webhooks fire, so we cannot shape the spike — the endpoint only authenticates and enqueues, letting workers smooth the processing rate.
whenOtherWins: 如果发布方需要在响应里立刻知道文章是否被接受（比如格式不合法要当场报错），同步处理才合适。
tradeoff: 快速 ACK 加异步处理的抗尖峰能力 vs 同步处理的即时反馈

termDefinitions.meaning: 确认响应，表示请求已被接收，不一定已经处理完。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An acknowledgement is a response confirming a request was received, though not necessarily finished.

optionExplanations: 对，代价是发布方拿到 200 时文章还没进 feed，接收成功不等于已生效。
同步做完意味着响应时间跟下游最慢的一环绑死，尖峰一来连接池先被占满。
推送方看到 5xx 通常会立刻重试，等于在最忙的时刻把流量又放大一轮。
限流会直接丢掉重大新闻本身，而这恰恰是我们最想第一时间拿到的内容。
optionExplanations_en: Right — the cost is that a 200 means received, not live, so the article is not in the feed yet.
Doing it synchronously ties response time to the slowest downstream stage, and a spike exhausts the connection pool first.
Senders usually retry immediately on a 5xx, which amplifies traffic exactly at the busiest moment.
Throttling drops the breaking story itself, which is precisely the content we most want the instant it appears.

scenario: webhook 采集要求每家发布方在自己的发布流程里加一次对我们接口的调用，很多小站没有工程团队。
scenario_en: Webhook ingestion asks each publisher to add a call to our endpoint inside their own publishing flow, and many small sites have no engineering team.
q: 为什么 webhook 不能当作唯一的采集方式？
q_en: Why can webhooks not be the only ingestion path?
options: 它要发布方主动改造，小站没有技术资源做这件事
webhook 推送的内容一定缺少标题和发布时间
HTTP POST 请求体不能携带文章正文这类长文本
webhook 到达的文章会绕过我们的地区划分逻辑
options_en: It requires publishers to change their own systems, and small sites lack the engineering resources.
Webhook payloads are always missing the title and publish time.
An HTTP POST body cannot carry long text like article content.
Articles arriving via webhook bypass our regional partitioning logic.
why: 轮询和抓取我们可以单方面上线，webhook 必须对方配合，覆盖率注定不满；所以它只能是最快的那一档，RSS 轮询和抓取仍要留着兜底。
why_en: Polling and scraping we can deploy unilaterally, but webhooks need the other side to cooperate, so coverage is never complete and the fallbacks must stay.
optionExplanations: 对，能不能拿到内容取决于对方愿不愿意排期，这是谈判问题不是技术问题。
推送体里放什么由我们定的契约决定，标题和时间戳正是必填字段。
POST 请求体可以携带完整正文，很多发布方推送时就是这么做的。
地区是我们在处理时按发布方属性打的，跟内容通过哪条通道进来无关。
optionExplanations_en: Right — whether we get the content depends on whether they will schedule the work, a negotiation problem rather than a technical one.
What the payload contains is defined by our contract, and title plus timestamp are exactly the required fields.
A POST body can carry full article text, and many publishers do send it that way.
Region is assigned by us from publisher attributes during processing, regardless of which channel delivered the content.

scenario: 缩略图存在 S3 上并生成了移动端、桌面端、高密屏三种尺寸，前面挂 CloudFront 做全球分发。
scenario_en: Thumbnails sit in S3 in mobile, desktop, and retina sizes, with CloudFront in front for global distribution.
q: 补全加了 CDN 之后的成本与延迟变化：
q_en: Fill in how cost and latency change once the CDN is added:
text: 回源请求数 = 总请求数 × (1 − 边缘命中率)。CloudFront 在边缘缓存后能把回源 S3 的请求减少 {{90%}} 以上，因此多存几种尺寸带来的存储成本被整体{{抵消}}，全球缩略图加载也进入 {{200ms}} 以内。
why: S3 egress 按请求和流量计费，命中率高到九成以上时这部分只剩十分之一，足以盖过多存两三份缩略图的存储费。
why_en: S3 egress is billed per request and per byte, so once the edge absorbs over ninety percent of them the remaining tenth easily outweighs a couple of extra thumbnail sizes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 内容分发网络：把静态文件缓存在离用户近的边缘节点上。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Content Delivery Network caches static files at edge locations close to users.

termDefinitions.meaning: 数据从云服务流出到互联网时按量收取的出网流量费。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Egress is the metered cost of data flowing out of a cloud service to the internet.

q: 把突发新闻扩容时的逐组件评估法排好序：
q_en: Put the per-component scaling evaluation in order:
steps: 先算这个组件在峰值时的资源需求是多少
对照现有设计判断它能不能满足这个需求
不满足就选对应的扩展手段：水平扩、加读副本或让缓存挡在前面
换下一个组件，用同样三步重新走一遍
why: 扩容不是笼统地"加机器"：对 Feed Service、数据库、Redis 逐个算峰值再决定手段，才能看出数据库其实是被缓存挡掉的，真正要扩的是缓存读吞吐。
why_en: Scaling is not a blanket add-more-servers: sizing Feed Service, database, and Redis one at a time reveals the cache absorbs the database load, so the real target is cache read throughput.

scenario: 团队不打算引入 Redis，但同样要让区域 feed 承接突发新闻期间的千万级并发读。
scenario_en: The team will not adopt Redis, yet the regional feed still has to absorb tens of millions of concurrent reads during breaking news.
q: 不用 Redis 时，等价的读扩展结构是什么？
q_en: Without Redis, what is the equivalent read-scaling structure?
options: 一致性哈希分片，每个分片再带一两个副本
把全部地区的 feed 都塞进单台大内存机器里
让每个应用实例各自缓存一份完整的区域 feed
干脆取消缓存层，所有 feed 读直接打到数据库
options_en: Shard with consistent hashing and give each shard one or two replicas.
Cram every region's feed into a single large-memory machine.
Let every application instance keep its own full copy of the regional feed.
Drop the cache layer entirely and send all feed reads to the database.
why: 关键结构不是 Redis 这个产品，而是"分片摊数据量、副本摊读吞吐并做故障转移"这一组；换成任何内存存储都照搬。代价是要自己运维这套分片。
why_en: The structure that matters is not Redis itself but sharding to spread data and replicas to spread reads and fail over, which transfers to any in-memory store.
whenOtherWins: 如果团队已经有 Redis 运维经验，直接用主从加 Sentinel 比自建一套分片省事得多。
tradeoff: 自建一致性哈希分片的可控性 vs 现成主从方案的运维成本

termDefinitions.meaning: 把 key 和节点映射到同一个环上的分片算法，增删节点时只搬动少量数据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Consistent hashing maps keys and nodes onto one ring so adding or removing a node moves only a small share of data.

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis 自带的高可用组件，负责监控主节点并在故障时提升副本。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Sentinel is the Redis high-availability component that watches the primary and promotes a replica on failure.

optionExplanations: 对，分片解决容量和写入分布，副本解决读吞吐和主节点挂掉后的接管。
单机内存再大也只有一份网卡和 CPU，读吞吐会先于容量撞上天花板。
每个实例各存一份就没有统一写入点，同一地区不同实例会给出不同 feed。
这正是引入缓存要解决的问题，撤掉之后数据库会被千万级读直接压垮。
optionExplanations_en: Right — shards spread capacity and writes, while replicas spread reads and take over when a primary dies.
However large one machine's memory is, it still has one NIC and one CPU, so read throughput hits the ceiling first.
A private copy per instance leaves no single write point, so two instances would serve different feeds for one region.
This is exactly the problem the cache exists to solve; removing it puts tens of millions of reads onto the database.

scenario: feed 读被负载均衡到多个 Redis 读副本上，主从之间是异步复制，延迟通常在 200ms 以内。
scenario_en: Feed reads are load-balanced across Redis read replicas with asynchronous replication that typically lags under 200ms.
q: 对新闻 feed 来说，这个复制延迟该怎么判断？
q_en: How should you judge that replication lag for a news feed?
options: 可接受，一条新闻晚 200ms 出现用户根本察觉不到
不可接受，所有 feed 读都必须回到主节点上去
不可接受，必须改成等所有副本确认的同步复制
不用管，异步复制不会让副本读到旧数据
options_en: Acceptable — a story appearing 200ms later is imperceptible to users.
Unacceptable — every feed read must go back to the primary.
Unacceptable — replication must become synchronous, waiting for all replicas.
Irrelevant — asynchronous replication never serves stale data from replicas.
why: 非功能需求里明确可用性优先于一致性，200ms 的滞后远小于用户对新闻新鲜度的感知阈值；换来的是读吞吐可以按副本数扩。
why_en: The requirements put availability ahead of consistency, and a 200ms lag sits far below what a news reader can perceive, buying read throughput that scales with replicas.
whenOtherWins: 如果读的是余额、库存这类必须读到自己刚写入的数据，就得走主节点或同步复制。
tradeoff: 读副本的吞吐扩展 vs 异步复制带来的短暂陈旧读
optionExplanations: 对，这正是"可用性优先于一致性"这条需求在具体数字上的兑现方式。
把读全压回主节点等于放弃了副本存在的意义，主节点马上成为吞吐瓶颈。
同步复制要等最慢的那个副本确认，写延迟被拉长，可用性反而下降。
异步复制期间副本上确实是旧值，只是这里的旧得不够久，影响不到体验。
optionExplanations_en: Right — this is what availability over consistency looks like once it is cashed out in real numbers.
Forcing all reads back to the primary defeats the purpose of replicas and makes the primary the bottleneck.
Synchronous replication waits for the slowest replica, stretching write latency and lowering availability instead.
Replicas genuinely do hold older values during async replication — the point is that here it is not old enough to matter.

scenario: 要支持 Sports、Politics、Tech 等分类 feed，文章在入库时就得带上 category 字段。
scenario_en: To support Sports, Politics, and Tech feeds, each article needs a category assigned at ingest time.
q: 入库时可以从哪些来源提取文章的 category？（多选）
q_en: Which sources can supply an article's category at ingest time? (Select all that apply.)
options: RSS feed 里发布方自己打的 <category> 标签
分析网页结构，从栏目路径或版块位置判断
对标题和正文做关键词匹配来归类
按发布方所在的国家和地区直接推断
options_en: The <category> tag the publisher already puts in the RSS feed.
Web page structure analysis, reading the section path or placement.
Keyword matching against the article title and body.
Inferring it directly from the publisher's country and region.
why: 优先用发布方已经标好的分类，缺失时才退到页面结构分析和关键词匹配；准确度依次下降，但覆盖率依次上升。
why_en: Prefer the category the publisher declared, and fall back to page structure and keyword matching only when it is missing — accuracy drops down that list while coverage rises.
optionExplanations: 发布方自己标的最准，拿来即用，省掉我们全部的推断成本。
栏目路径反映的是站点自己的编辑分类，比猜内容语义可靠得多。
关键词是覆盖没有任何结构线索的来源的兜底，代价是会误判一部分。
地区和分类是两个正交维度，同一个地区的发布方什么题材都发。
optionExplanations_en: What the publisher declared is the most accurate and free to use, sparing us any inference cost.
A section path reflects the site's own editorial taxonomy, far more reliable than guessing semantics.
Keywords are the fallback for sources with no structural hints, at the price of some misclassification.
Region and category are orthogonal dimensions — publishers in one region cover every topic there is.

scenario: 区域缓存里存的是完整文章 JSON（含 category 字段），分类请求靠读回整段缓存再在应用里过滤。
scenario_en: The regional cache stores full article JSON including a category field, and category requests read the whole cache back and filter in the application.
q: 补全内存过滤路径的耗时构成和它支撑的判断：
q_en: Fill in the latency breakdown of in-memory filtering and the decision it supports:
text: 总耗时 = 缓存读取 + 应用内过滤：从 Redis 读回最近 1000 篇缓存文章约 {{10ms}} 以内，按 category 过滤再加 {{1-2ms}}，合起来远低于 {{200ms}} 这个给定的 feed 延迟目标。
why: 200ms 是产品给定的 SLO，不是算出来的；这里十几毫秒的实测说明余量充足，因此不必为 25 个分类乘 10 个地区维护 250 个缓存键。
why_en: The 200ms figure is a given service level objective rather than a derived result, and a dozen milliseconds of headroom justifies not maintaining 250 separate category cache keys.

termDefinitions.meaning: 服务等级目标：团队对外承诺的延迟或可用性指标。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Service Level Objective is the latency or availability target a team commits to.

scenario: 个性化排序需要一份用户画像，排序函数本身是 ML 模型，这里只关心喂给它的信号。
scenario_en: Personalized ranking needs a user profile; the scoring function itself is an ML model, so only its input signals matter here.
q: 构建用户画像时会用到哪些信号？（多选）
q_en: Which signals go into building a user profile? (Select all that apply.)
options: 用户显式订阅的主题和偏好的发布方
点击、阅读时长、分享这类行为数据
协同过滤得出的相似用户的阅读偏好
用户设备当前的电池电量和存储余量
options_en: Topics the user explicitly subscribed to and publishers they prefer.
Behavioral data such as clicks, reading time, and shares.
Preferences of similar users derived from collaborative filtering.
The device's current battery level and remaining storage.
why: 画像由显式偏好和行为信号两类构成，再用协同过滤补上"读过 A 和 B 的人也读 C"；三者一起决定文章的相关性分数。
why_en: A profile combines explicit preferences with behavioral signals, then collaborative filtering adds the readers-of-A-and-B-also-read-C pattern to set relevance scores.

termDefinitions.meaning: 根据"和你行为相似的人还喜欢什么"来推荐内容的方法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Collaborative filtering recommends content based on what users with similar behavior also engaged with.

termDefinitions.meaning: 机器学习，这里指给文章打相关性分数的排序模型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Machine Learning here refers to the ranking model that scores articles for relevance.

optionExplanations: 显式偏好是用户自己说出口的意图，最可靠也最不用猜。
行为信号补上用户没说但真实在读的部分，比自述更贴近实际兴趣。
协同过滤能推出新兴趣，帮新用户越过冷启动阶段。
电量和存储属于设备状态，跟这个人想读什么题材毫无关联。
optionExplanations_en: Explicit preferences are intent the user stated outright — the most reliable input, with no guessing.
Behavioral signals capture what they actually read but never said, closer to real interest than self-report.
Collaborative filtering surfaces new interests and helps new users past the cold-start stage.
Battery and storage are device state and say nothing about what topics this person wants to read.

scenario: 注册用户里只有一部分每天都来，但给全部用户都预计算个性化 feed 的内存扛不住。
scenario_en: Only some registered users show up daily, yet precomputing a personalized feed for all of them does not fit in memory.
q: 预计算和按需生成该怎么在用户之间分配？
q_en: How should precomputation and on-demand generation be split across users?
options: 活跃用户预计算，不活跃用户按需从分类缓存现拼
所有用户一律预计算，靠不断加内存来解决问题
所有用户一律按需生成，彻底放弃预计算这条路
按注册时间的先后来决定谁能享受预计算待遇
options_en: Precompute for active users and assemble on demand from category caches for inactive ones.
Precompute for everyone and keep adding memory to cope.
Generate everything on demand and abandon precomputation entirely.
Decide who gets precomputation by how early they registered.
why: 预计算的成本随用户数线性上涨，收益却只落在真会来的人身上；按活跃度分层把内存花在会被读到的 feed 上。代价是不活跃用户回归时首刷慢一点。
why_en: Precomputation costs scale with user count while the benefit only lands on users who return, so tiering by activity spends memory on feeds that actually get read.
whenOtherWins: 如果绝大多数注册用户每天都活跃，分层就没有意义，全量预计算反而更简单。
tradeoff: 预计算换来的读延迟 vs 随用户规模线性增长的内存成本
optionExplanations: 对，判断依据是这份 feed 被读到的概率，而不是这个用户是否存在。
内存随注册人数线性上涨而利用率很低，等于长期为不会被读的数据付费。
每次都现拼会让活跃用户的每一次刷新都承担组装开销，最热的路径最慢。
注册早晚跟他今天会不会来毫无关系，拿它分层等于随机分配内存。
optionExplanations_en: Right — the criterion is the probability this feed gets read, not whether the user exists.
Memory grows linearly with the user base at very low utilization, paying indefinitely for data nobody reads.
Assembling every time makes every refresh by an active user pay assembly cost, so the hottest path is slowest.
Registration date says nothing about whether they show up today, so tiering on it allocates memory at random.

scenario: 重大突发新闻发生，但很多用户的偏好向量里根本没有这个主题的权重。
scenario_en: A major story breaks, but many users' preference vectors carry no weight for that topic at all.
q: 混合组装的个性化 feed 怎么保证这条新闻能被看到？
q_en: How does a mix-assembled personalized feed make sure that story is seen?
options: 临时上调 trending 权重，压低个人偏好权重
把所有用户的偏好向量清空之后重新学习一遍
为这条突发新闻单独建一份覆盖全部用户的缓存
完全不做处理，等用户自己去分类页里慢慢翻到这条新闻
options_en: Temporarily raise the trending category weight and lower personal preference weights.
Wipe every user's preference vector and relearn from scratch.
Build a dedicated cache of this one story covering every single user.
Do nothing and let users find the story by browsing category pages.
why: 既然 feed 就是按比例混合几个分类缓存，突发期直接改这组比例是最省事的开关；代价是这段时间个性化被稀释，所有人的 feed 更接近通用 feed。
why_en: Since the feed is just a weighted mix of category caches, changing the weights is the cheapest switch during breaking news, at the cost of diluting personalization.
whenOtherWins: 平时没有全局要闻的时候，保持原比例才能让个性化真正发挥作用。
tradeoff: 突发期的全局重要性 vs 平时的个性化深度
optionExplanations: 对，调权重是全局配置改动，不用碰任何一个用户的数据就能立刻生效。
清空画像会把所有人打回冷启动，为了一条新闻毁掉长期积累的信号。
给上亿用户各写一份，正是这套方案当初为了省内存要避开的做法。
突发新闻的价值全在时效，等用户主动去找等于放弃了这份价值。
optionExplanations_en: Right — weights are a global config change that takes effect immediately without touching any user's data.
Wiping profiles resets everyone to cold start, destroying long-accumulated signal for the sake of one story.
Writing a copy for hundreds of millions of users is exactly the memory blowup this design was built to avoid.
A breaking story's value is entirely in timeliness, so waiting for users to hunt for it throws that value away.

scenario: feed 按 region 分区预计算缓存，但大量用户没登录，也从来没设置过自己的地区。
scenario_en: Feeds are precomputed per region, yet many users are anonymous and have never set a region.
q: 匿名用户的 region 字段该怎么确定？
q_en: How should the region field be determined for anonymous users?
options: 按请求来源 IP 推断一个默认值，允许用户显式覆盖
统一给所有匿名用户发全球混合 feed，不区分地区
强制要求先注册登录才能看到任何 feed 内容
随机分配一个地区缓存，反正后面会慢慢修正过来
options_en: Infer a default from the request IP and let the user override it explicitly.
Serve all anonymous users one global mixed feed with no regional split.
Require registration and login before showing any feed content at all.
Assign a random region cache and assume it gets corrected later.
why: region 是决定读哪个预计算缓存键的路由字段，每个请求都必须有值，所以匿名用户也要有轻量档案；代价是 VPN 和跨境用户会先拿到错的地区。
why_en: Region routes the request to a precomputed cache key, so every request needs one and even anonymous users get a lightweight profile.
whenOtherWins: 如果用户经常跨境或长期用 VPN，让他显式选择地区比 IP 推断可靠得多。
tradeoff: IP 推断的零摩擦 vs 显式设置的准确性

termDefinitions.meaning: 网络地址，可以粗略映射到访问者所在的国家或城市。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An Internet Protocol address is a network address that maps roughly to the visitor's country or city.

termDefinitions.meaning: 虚拟专用网络，会让请求看起来来自另一个国家。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Virtual Private Network makes requests appear to originate from another country.

optionExplanations: 对，推断给默认值、设置做覆盖，这样第一次访问就能命中某个区域缓存。
全球混合会让美国用户第一屏看到大量无关的外国本地新闻，相关性崩掉。
强制登录会挡掉聚合器最大的一部分流量，为一个可推断字段付出太多。
随机地区意味着首屏内容和用户毫无关系，而且没有任何机制去修正它。
optionExplanations_en: Right — inference supplies the default and settings override it, so even a first visit hits some regional cache.
A global mix fills a US reader's first screen with irrelevant foreign local news, collapsing relevance.
Forcing login blocks the largest slice of an aggregator's traffic, a steep price for a field we can infer.
A random region makes the first screen unrelated to the user, with no mechanism to ever correct it.
